sunless-citadel.title: The first road led down
opening: Before the long roads, the distant planes, and the names that would return to haunt them, there was Oakhurst—and a family waiting for news. The Hucreles had lost adventurers to the Sunless Citadel. Shrop and Terry helped strike the bargain to find them. With Thunder at their side, they took up a search that would leave them with far more than a reward.

Before Oakhurst, Thunder’s road had brought him to the Stolen Sons. Sent to work for them after being caught burgling a house, he met Terry and Shrop there. The name belonged to the company’s beginnings long before it would return in the stories of Brindinford and the captives beneath the earth.
A broken fortress lay beneath the earth. Somewhere in its dark were the missing, the truth behind a strange harvest, and the first threads of a story that would follow Team Biscuit for years.

scenes.title: A less than graceful entrance
paragraphs: The Citadel wasted little time making its introductions. Shrop met the giant rats—and a pit trap. Thunder began the quieter work of disarming traps, finding hidden doors, and opening locks. It was an early glimpse of a useful arrangement: Shrop could survive the sort of discovery everyone preferred Thunder to make first.

Terry kept his companions alive and made liberal use of chalk. The work was practical, sometimes inelegant, and entirely necessary. Great adventures require courage. They also benefit from someone remembering which way the party came.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the ravine above the buried Citadel
image.caption: The way into the Sunless Citadel.

scenes.title: Steel, chalk, and a little diplomacy
paragraphs: Not every obstacle called for the same answer. Shrop dealt with Caltrop Hall by breaking down the door and charging the defences. Elsewhere, the company freed Erky Timbers and persuaded the goblin chief to agree to a truce. They could fight their way through a door; they could also recognise when a conversation might open one.

The search began to reveal a second danger. Terry connected Belak’s mutations with the mystery of the apple and the twig blights. The troubles below the Citadel had roots reaching beyond its walls. Returning with news of the missing would not be enough if Oakhurst remained unaware of what threatened it.

hindsight.title: A harvest meant to spread
paragraphs: Belak’s fruit was a means of colonisation. He ordered the goblins to scatter its seeds aboveground; their decision to sell the apples still served his purpose. Each planted seed could become a twig blight. The apparent blessing offered to Oakhurst carried the next infestation inside it.

scenes.title: The fourth familiar name
paragraphs: Grim had already been adventuring on his own. It was in the Citadel that the others found him, with Shrop the first to discover the gnome who would become so much a part of their story.

He brought a familiar’s scouting, a growing store of magical knowledge, and an opinion about how to handle the people they had come to find. When the company confronted the missing adventurers, Grim urged that they be subdued. Shrop and Thunder helped put that choice into practice. The search had brought them to a confrontation; they chose restraint.

There were quieter beginnings, too. Grim began teaching Terry Draconic. Their translations helped the company make sense of books, scrolls, and the Citadel’s dragon lore. Shrop and Thunder had encountered the name Ashardalon early in the expedition; Grim had learned something of the dragon even before his own adventures began. It was a name the campaign would not let them forget.

Grim’s hunger for knowledge had a particular ambition behind it: to gather all known magic into a single great tome. Every recovered text, unfamiliar inscription, and new spell could become another part of that life’s work. The company had found a wizard for whom a discovery could be as compelling as a treasure chest.

scenes.title: What the darkness left them
paragraphs: Shrop recovered Shatterspike. Grim braved the dragon fountain. When troll parts needed burning, Grim supplied the reminder and Terry supplied the follow-through. Shrop resisted the lure of enchanted music and discovered Jot. There was danger in grand discoveries and in the smaller details the party could ill afford to overlook.

Beneath it all lay the mystery of Belak’s work and the sinister growth associated with the Gulthias Tree. The Citadel had given the company more than enemies to overcome: it had given them questions worth carrying back into the light.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the Twilight Grove beneath the Citadel
image.caption: The Twilight Grove, beneath the ruined fortress.

hindsight.title: The tree, the stake, and the stolen will
paragraphs: The Gulthias Tree had grown from a stake used to pin a vampire to this place. Sharwyn and Sir Braford had become its thralls, absorbed and remade to serve the tree and its keeper. The company’s choice to subdue them was made against a horror that had already reached far beyond ordinary captivity. The dark growth was another legacy of undeath in a story that would lead back to Gulthias.

scenes.title: The rings came home
paragraphs: The company returned the Hucrele rings and brought back news of every missing adventurer. The bargain in Oakhurst could finally be answered, though an answer was not the same thing as a happy ending. Shrop urged the party to attend the funeral. Their first adventure closed with remembrance as well as reward.

They also warned the town about the twig blights. What they had learned in the dark mattered to people who would never descend into it. The expedition had become more than a search for a missing party: it had made these adventurers responsible for what they now knew.

By the end, Thunder had also shared his lycanthropy with the company. The dangers they would face were not all waiting behind the next locked door. Some would travel with them—and become part of the trust that held them together.

companions.title: Four names for the road ahead

people.name: Shrop
people.text: First through danger, bearer of Shatterspike, and the companion who remembered that the dead deserved a funeral.

people.name: Grim
people.text: A solo adventurer who became a companion, a teacher, and a voice for restraint when the missing were finally found.

people.name: Terry
people.text: Healer, translator in training, solver of the apple’s mystery, and firm believer in the practical value of chalk.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: Finder of traps and hidden ways, deft with a lock, and learning to trust the company with a danger of his own.

closing.title: Another name, another road
paragraphs: Terry had learned the legend of Durgeddin the Black. Beyond Oakhurst lay the promise of a dwarven smith’s lost works and the road toward Blasingdell. The next adventure would lead into Khundrukar, the ruined stronghold remembered as the Forge of Fury.
The company carried its first hard-earned lessons with it: the value of an opened door, a stayed blade, a translated word, and a companion willing to stand in front.

forge-of-fury.title: What waited beneath the Stone Tooth
opening: The legend of Durgeddin the Black had given the company a new direction. From the mining town of Blasingdell, the road led toward the Stone Tooth: a steep height above a dwarven stronghold long lost to its makers. Khundrukar promised the work of a master smith. Reaching it would demand rather more than an appreciation of fine craftsmanship.
The journey began with wolves and orcs. Ahead lay guarded doors, underground rivers, the Glitterhame, and the old dwarf-halls. This time, all four companions were on the road together.

scenes.title: The door was only the beginning
paragraphs: The approach to Khundrukar was watched. Grim discovered the murder holes, and Shrop helped work out the danger of the entrance. The company fought through the archers’ positions, with Terry tending the wounded. Beyond the Dwarf-Door, a rope bridge hung over the rift. Thunder was the first across.

The habits formed in the Citadel were becoming dependable ones. Grim found secret ways. Terry marked the route in chalk. Shrop opened most of the doors—and, at the dwarven statue, triggered a trap that Thunder then put right. It was a practical division of labour, if occasionally a painful one.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the rope bridge spanning the rift in Khundrukar
image.caption: The crossing inside the Mountain Door. Thunder went first.

scenes.title: Two lives worth turning back for
paragraphs: Among the orcs’ prisoners, the party found the twins. They freed them, then made arrangements to get them out of the mountain. Terry and Thunder escorted the rescued prisoners to the cart and planned for its return in three days. Shrop and Grim remained behind to explore and rest.

The rescue gave their expedition a responsibility beyond whatever treasure Durgeddin had left. A wagon’s return mattered. So did the distance back to safety. Terry worked out the cart’s schedule while the company continued its descent, counting more than the doors still unopened.

Great Ulfe and the wolves Vak and Thrag fell to the company. So did the shaman Burdurg. The upper stronghold had tested their coordination; the Grand Stair now offered them a way deeper into the mountain.

scenes.title: The light beneath the mountain
paragraphs: Below the defended halls, Khundrukar opened into the Glitterhame. Fungi and pale light gave the caverns a beauty quite different from the stronghold above. Running water threaded through the darkness; dwarven sepulchers stood among the stone formations. The company had found a place where the mountain’s history and its living dangers occupied the same ground.

They fought through the troglodytes and their chieftain Kaarghaz. Terry continued his search into dwarven history and recovered Gharin’s Warhammer. Grim pursued his own questions about Ashardalon, collecting oddments and discoveries along the way. Shrop and Thunder had the Stolen Sons to reckon with as another thread running through their travels.

The party did not simply press on without pause. They returned to the wagon and to Blasingdell, rested, and gathered themselves before going back into Khundrukar. The road out of the mountain was part of the adventure, too.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of the fungal growth in the Glitterhame
image.caption: The Glitterhame: strange beauty below the old stronghold.

scenes.title: Other hands at Durgeddin’s forge
paragraphs: The old halls were occupied. Duergar worked at the forges, and the company met them with steel, spells, and questions. Shatterspike served Shrop against the gray dwarves. The party questioned duergar for clues, making the ruined stronghold a source of answers as well as danger.

Beyond the Great Hall and the Bladeworks, the rooms still bore the marks of Khundrukar’s fall. Defaced carvings, abandoned quarters, and the remains of old warriors surrounded the living intruders. The company was searching for Durgeddin’s legacy inside the wreckage of the world that had made it.

image.alt: Original adventure illustration of duergar in Khundrukar
image.caption: The gray dwarves had put the ruined stronghold to work again.

scenes.title: The dead, the disguised, and the furniture
paragraphs: The dwarf-halls had dangers for which an ordinary door was inadequate warning. A ghost turned its attention on Thunder; Shrop helped work out more of that encounter’s mystery. In a room of books, the sorrowful old man the party encountered concealed a very different nature. Idalla was a succubus, and the company defeated her.

Nor could they rely on furnishings to remain furnishings. Animated armor, a smothering rug, and even a kitchen table joined the mountain’s opposition. There are grander indignities in an adventurer’s life, but being attacked by the furniture deserves its own place in the telling.

The way onward demanded ingenuity as well as endurance. Grim put Levitate to work at the chain ladder. Terry’s healing had helped keep the company moving through the expedition. Below, the river led toward the Black Lake.

hindsight.title: Idalla’s curse was a lie
paragraphs: Idalla’s tale of a curse that would kill intruders after three days and a night was invented. So was the claim that three of Durgeddin’s weapons were needed to break it, and the warning about a doppelganger in the Glitterhame. She mixed those lies with real history and a real haunting. Even her dragon warning exaggerated a young Nightscale into an ancient terror.

hindsight.title: Why the furniture fought
paragraphs: Arundil had escaped the orcs’ final assault, then returned to find his people slaughtered. Grief drove him to animate dead warriors and household objects against future intruders. He also summoned the fiend who killed him. The ghost, the deadly furnishings, and Idalla were remnants of the same desperate attempt to defend a home that had already fallen.

scenes.title: Nightscale
paragraphs: Grim was the first to see Nightscale. Thunder crept close to the dragon, and Shrop drew first blood. The young black dragon was the final great threat waiting in Khundrukar’s depths, beside the dark water and the promise of a hoard.

The company defeated Nightscale. After the orcs, the prisoners, the forges, the hauntings, and the long descent, all four had earned a new experience to set beside their first adventure: they had faced a dragon and survived.

The hoard lay on an island in the lake. Durgeddin’s stronghold had drawn them with the promise of lost riches, but its deepest cavern had demanded that they prove themselves before it yielded anything at all.

image.alt: Original Forge of Fury cover illustration of a black dragon above an underground chasm
image.caption: Nightscale, the black dragon beneath Khundrukar.

people.name: Shrop
people.text: Opened the way, brought Shatterspike against the duergar, and struck the first blow against Nightscale.

people.name: Grim
people.text: Found murder holes and hidden doors, made inventive use of Levitate, and first saw the dragon waiting below.

people.name: Terry
people.text: Helped bring the twins to safety, recovered Gharin’s Warhammer, and kept chalk and healing close at hand.

people.name: Thunder
people.text: First across the rope bridge, escort to the rescued twins, finder of traps, and bold enough to sneak up on Nightscale.

closing.title: Brindinford awaited
paragraphs: Beyond Khundrukar, the road led to Brindinford. The company arrived as the town’s fair filled the streets with halfling travellers, merchants, entertainers, and the bustle of a celebration. After the mountain’s dark halls, there were stalls to explore and a town full of people to meet.

They had come out of the Forge of Fury as a company that could cross a chasm, arrange a rescue, unpick a deception, and bring down a dragon. Brindinford would ask what they could do when the danger was hidden in a crowded town.

fungal-bloom.title: From the grotto to sunken Brindinford
opening: Team Biscuit’s journey home from Icewind Dale led into the story of another company: Team Gravy. Brunn Ironbelly, Rook Kestrel, Nox Veyra, and Elira Moss-Weaver had a darkness of their own to explore. Their road would join Team Biscuit’s in a place the older company had every reason to remember: Brindinford.

Their side of the tale led to an old stronghold along an underground river. Its former occupants had left bones, broken weapons, and abandoned rooms. Something far more persistent had taken their place. Fungus covered the stone, spread across the water, and hung in the air itself.

Beyond the fungal stronghold lay a buried city and a different struggle. Here, the two companies fought together against giant ants through streets where Team Biscuit had once helped restore a fair, a temple, and a town’s freedom.

scenes.title: Passage aboard the Deliverance
paragraphs: Team Gravy’s approach to the grotto came aboard the Deliverance, among spectral sailors still attending to their old duties. Captain Pepper kept the ship’s course while Xanthar directed the expedition. Beneath the ship lay a river winding through a landscape of ruined bridges and scorched stone.

At the Brindinford cut, Xanthar pointed out the fissure leading towards the grotto. A smaller boat would take the adventurers in. He supplied the word Freeher to make the water recede, set a twenty-four-hour return window, and asked them to bring back a map. If they found a portal, they were to return immediately.

The Anchor’s light lowered them towards the river and the smell of fungus. The mission began with a ship waiting above, a boat below, and a deadline measured against the returning water. What lay in the stronghold would make the journey out considerably less orderly.

image.alt: Campaign portrait of Captain Timothy Pepper in his ornate naval coat and hat
image.caption: Captain Pepper of the Deliverance, whose ship carried more than ordinary passengers.

scenes.title: A ruin that had learned to grow
paragraphs: The grotto’s corruption was alive. Green and black mold clung to the old rooms; red mushrooms scattered spores; stranger growths flashed in the darkness. Water offered no simple refuge. Even a breath could carry the sickness that had claimed the stronghold.

Its victims became part of the infestation. The dead hobgoblins were not merely warnings left behind by a lost garrison: necromantic spores could put their bodies back to work. A ruined fortress is troublesome enough when its occupants have the decency to remain dead.

image.alt: Campaign artwork of a cavern overgrown with luminous fungi
image.caption: The fungal dark of Team Gravy’s detour.

scenes.title: The old traps still worked
paragraphs: The fungus had not replaced the stronghold’s older cruelties. Concealed pits could fill with water. Electrified floors protected cages. Illusions offered interesting things to investigate in precisely the places where a curious adventurer might wish they had been less curious.

Beyond a hidden door waited a chamber of spinning blades and numbered switches. The answer was bound up with an inscription on the old hobgoblin ruler’s throne. Here, surviving the living growth meant paying attention to the dead inhabitants’ puzzles, too.

scenes.title: Unusual company
paragraphs: The grotto was not entirely without conversation. Prigs, Blip, and Zonkatofu were goblins with stolen goods, a shared pipe, and a spectacularly poor approach to testing the local spores. Their claim that smoking the fungus granted truesight was best understood as an advertisement from three deeply unreliable experts.

Other figures in the stronghold wore hobgoblin shapes while pursuing purposes of their own. Their interest in the infestation and its source made them part of the same struggle, though appearances alone could not tell the company whom it had found.
A friendly face, a ridiculous offer, a hidden purpose: even far from the main company’s road, the campaign had found familiar ways to make a room more complicated than it first appeared.

hindsight.title: Angels in hobgoblin shapes
paragraphs: Duma, Sabrael, Jael, and the other disguised devas were celestials trying to stop the planar infestation. The forbiddance around the gate-room kept them out, giving mortal explorers an opening their power could not overcome. Hayyel, the planetar, carried a harsher solution: destroy the entire complex if the gate could not be stopped. The apparently strange company inside the ruin included a celestial mission under a deadline.

scenes.title: The wound behind the growth
paragraphs: At the heart of the infestation stood a planar gate. The fungus had entered the world through that opening, and the gate had horrors of its own: dark tendrils could draw a living creature into a pocket of darkness and despair. Clearing a corridor would never be enough while the source remained.

The blade Shokkurg’s Fang offered a means of destroying the gate. The celestials faced another obstacle: the chamber’s ward barred them from entering. Their power could bring them into the grotto, but it could not carry them through that final doorway.

Hayyel had prepared a desperate alternative. If the gate remained open, the stockpile of flammable liquid could bring the whole complex down. The grotto’s central danger was larger than any one monster: a spreading corruption, a guarded way to its source, and a remedy that could destroy the very place it sought to cleanse.

scenes.title: A wish, a falling boat, and a ghostly rescue
paragraphs: The escape from the grotto tore open into a new danger. A wish carried the boat out into empty air above Brindinford Falls. The goblins clung to Rook in the hope that his wings might save them, while the boat and its passengers fell towards the white water.

Then the Deliverance appeared alongside them. The smaller craft crashed onto its deck, where the spectral crew moved to secure it. Xanthar pressed the passengers to take the waiting sacks of payment and supplies, then return to the boat. Captain Pepper brought the ship round towards the cliff.

At the last instant, the Deliverance vanished. The boat was thrown back into the underground river, where the current seized it and carried it into the narrowing dark. The rescue had exchanged a fall over the waterfall for another passage beneath the earth. Beyond the grotto lay the buried city and the fight the two companies would share.

scenes.title: Beyond the grotto: two companies in the dark
paragraphs: Escaping the Fungal Grotto brought the adventurers beneath Faerûn and into the long-lost ruins of Brindinford. Team Biscuit and Team Gravy now shared the fight for a way through. Shrop, Grim, Terry, and Thunder stood alongside Brunn, Rook, Nox, and Elira in the buried remains of a town that had once welcomed music and crowds.

The cavern had swallowed the streets. Ash and broken stone lay across the old routes; warm vents and volcanic fire marked fractures in the earth. Shelter had to be won, and moving from one ruined district to the next meant finding a passage that the colony did not already hold.
The grotto’s escape had brought them to another battlefield. Both companies would need to survive it together.

scenes.title: The ants held the streets
paragraphs: The colony moved through collapsed houses, tunnels, and the passages beneath the town. Its attacks were coordinated, its numbers relentless. The old walls and narrow ways made every advance costly; an opening through the rubble could be a route forward or another place for the ants to close around them.

There were soldiers and spitters, enormous ant behemoths, and swarms that turned the ground itself into a threat. Burrowing swarms struck from below; devouring swarms filled the ruined lanes. The colony also had brood-medic swarms among its forces. The two companies were fighting an enemy with more ways to sustain the pressure than a single great monster could offer.

They fought street by street for days. By 15 Kythorn, 1407 DR, the survivors had reached the old barracks district. It was hard-won ground in a city where every pause and every route ahead still had to be considered against the next attack.

hindsight.title: The hand behind the colony
paragraphs: The deeper hive concealed a neogi master and a queen bound into a system of resonance and control. Barbed filaments and foreign devices threaded through the ruins, directing a colony whose discipline exceeded ordinary animal instinct. The bell tower formed the centre of that hidden apparatus. While the survivors scouted the Wrinkle, the will directing the colony waited deeper in the ruins.

scenes.title: The town Team Biscuit remembered
paragraphs: Brindinford’s names had survived its ruin. The manor, the market, the smithy, the temple, the Stony Gaze, and the bell tower belonged to the same town Team Biscuit had known during The Speaker in Dreams. Once, those streets had held the Halfling Faire. The company had cleansed Pelor’s temple, freed the Baron, and left with food and seed for Ossington. Now the familiar plan lay buried beneath ash and stone.

For Team Gravy, the fallen town was part of the expedition they had joined. For Team Biscuit, it also held places where they had fought, rested, and been celebrated. The shared struggle carried the weight of that earlier rescue into a town whose surviving buildings offered little comfort.

From the barracks, familiars scouted ahead into the old Magical District. Much of it had collapsed: streets choked with rubble, broken towers leaning into the cavern walls, and fire showing through cracks below. One building remained intact. The Reality Wrinkle was still standing.

image.alt: Earlier overview map of Brindinford, showing the town’s landmarks before its fall
image.caption: Brindinford before its fall: the familiar landmarks of The Speaker in Dreams.

closing.title: The silence at the Reality Wrinkle
paragraphs: The old shop had belonged to Those Who Hear, the cult tied to the gibbering-mouther horrors of Team Biscuit’s earlier visit. Around it, the Magical District had fallen apart. No lights burned there, and the scouts saw no movement. Its survival left the company with a destination and another uneasy question.

Team Biscuit and Team Gravy pushed towards the Wrinkle in search of answers, supplies, forgotten magic, or a way onward through the Sunken City. Behind them lay the grotto and the streets they had fought to cross. Ahead stood a familiar doorway in an unfamiliar darkness, with the colony still pressing through the ruins.

Beyond that still-unanswered doorway lay the older reckoning. The Cathezar’s pursuit, Thunder’s connection to Dydd, the secrets of Rigus, and the children born without souls had survived every detour. Ashardalon’s name had followed Team Biscuit since the Citadel. The journey stood on the threshold of returning to that unfinished struggle in Bastion of Broken Souls.
